name: Barbell Bench Press
steps: Lie flat on the bench with eyes directly beneath the racked barbell. Plant feet flat and drive into the floor.
Grip the bar just wider than shoulder-width with wrists straight. Retract and depress scapulae firmly against bench pad.
Unrack the bar and stabilize it directly over sternum with locked elbows and braced core.
Lower bar in controlled diagonal arc touching mid-sternum while maintaining 45 to 70 degree elbow angle.
Drive bar forcefully up and slightly back toward shoulder joint line to full lockout.
mistakes: Flaring elbows outward at a 90-degree angle, causing shoulder impingement and anterior rotator cuff stress.
Bouncing the resistance violently off the chest instead of utilizing a controlled eccentric stretch.
Over-arching the lumbar spine and lifting glutes completely off the bench.
formTips: Lie flat on the bench with eyes directly beneath the racked barbell. Plant feet flat and drive into the floor.

name: Machine Chest Press
steps: Adjust seat height so machine handles align with mid-chest level.
Plant feet firmly flat on floor and press upper back and hips into backrest pad.
Grasp handles with firm grip and press outward smoothly along fixed guided motion path until arms extend without elbow hyperextension.
Pause for 1 second at peak pectoral contraction.
Control eccentric return with 2-3s tempo back until chest reaches deep comfortable stretch.
mistakes: Flaring elbows outward at a 90-degree angle, causing shoulder impingement and anterior rotator cuff stress.
Bouncing the resistance violently off the chest instead of utilizing a controlled eccentric stretch.
Over-arching the lumbar spine and lifting glutes completely off the bench.
formTips: Adjust seat height so machine handles align with mid-chest level.

name: Incline Machine Chest Press
steps: Adjust seat so handles sit right at upper clavicular chest level.
Drive shoulder blades down and back against 30-degree angled backrest pad.
Press handles upward and forward targeting upper pectoralis major.
Squeeze upper chest hard at peak lockout.
Lower weights slowly under controlled eccentric stretch.
mistakes: Flaring elbows outward at a 90-degree angle, causing shoulder impingement and anterior rotator cuff stress.
Bouncing the resistance violently off the chest instead of utilizing a controlled eccentric stretch.
Over-arching the lumbar spine and lifting glutes completely off the bench.
formTips: Adjust seat so handles sit right at upper clavicular chest level.

name: Decline Machine Chest Press
steps: Sit in decline chest press machine with hips back against lumbar support pad.
Grasp handles with neutral or pronated grip aligned with lower chest line.
Press downward and forward along machine arc until arms are extended.
Squeeze lower sternal head of chest at full extension.
Return slowly to starting stretch position.
mistakes: Flaring elbows outward at a 90-degree angle, causing shoulder impingement and anterior rotator cuff stress.
Bouncing the resistance violently off the chest instead of utilizing a controlled eccentric stretch.
Over-arching the lumbar spine and lifting glutes completely off the bench.
formTips: Sit in decline chest press machine with hips back against lumbar support pad.

name: Pec Deck (Machine Chest Fly)
steps: Adjust seat so elbow pads or handles align horizontally with mid-sternum.
Rest forearms against pads or hold handles with a slight soft bend in elbows.
Squeeze chest muscles to bring pads/handles together in front of sternum in smooth arc.
Hold peak isometric squeeze hard for 1-2 seconds.
Return under complete control feeling deep pectoral eccentric stretch.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Adjust seat so elbow pads or handles align horizontally with mid-sternum.

name: Machine Shoulder Press
steps: Adjust seat height so handles sit at ear height.
Press back firmly against pad and brace core.
Press handles straight overhead along machine track until arms extend.
Pause briefly overhead without shrugging traps excessively.
Lower weights smoothly down to ear level.
mistakes: Flaring elbows outward at a 90-degree angle, causing shoulder impingement and anterior rotator cuff stress.
Bouncing the resistance violently off the chest instead of utilizing a controlled eccentric stretch.
Over-arching the lumbar spine and lifting glutes completely off the bench.
formTips: Adjust seat height so handles sit at ear height.

name: Machine Lateral Raise
steps: Sit upright on lateral raise machine with chest against support pad.
Rest outer arms against padded levers with elbows bent at 90 degrees.
Raise elbows outward and upward using lateral deltoids until upper arms reach parallel.
Hold peak contraction at top for 1 full second.
Slowly lower arms back to starting position resisting the weight stack.
mistakes: Using excessive momentum and swinging the torso.
Leading with the hands instead of elbows, engaging the upper traps excessively.
formTips: Sit upright on lateral raise machine with chest against support pad.

name: Rear Delt Machine (Reverse Pec Deck)
steps: Sit facing the pec deck machine pad with chest flat against backrest.
Hold handles with neutral or pronated grip and elbows soft.
Drive arms back horizontally in wide arc focusing purely on posterior deltoids.
Contract rear delts hard at full retraction.
Return slowly to forward starting position.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Sit facing the pec deck machine pad with chest flat against backrest.

name: Plate-Loaded Lat Pulldown Machine
steps: Adjust thigh pad snug against tops of thighs while sitting on seat.
Grasp divergent handles with wide overhead grip.
Pull handles downward and inward driving elbows towards hip pockets.
Squeeze lats tight at bottom of stroke.
Allow handles to travel back up fully stretching latissimus dorsi.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Adjust thigh pad snug against tops of thighs while sitting on seat.

name: Seated Machine Row
steps: Adjust chest pad so arms can reach handles with full forward extension.
Sit upright, brace chest against pad, and grab handles.
Retract shoulder blades and pull elbows back past torso.
Squeeze rhomboids and middle back muscles firmly.
Extend arms slowly back to full forward stretch.
mistakes: Yanking with lower back momentum rather than initiating with active scapular retraction.
Shrugging shoulders into the neck rather than pulling elbows down toward the hip pockets.
formTips: Adjust chest pad so arms can reach handles with full forward extension.

name: Chest-Supported T-Bar Row Machine
steps: Lie face down on inclined chest support pad with feet hooked securely on platform.
Grasp T-bar handles with overhand or neutral grip.
Pull elbows up and back driving through upper back and lats without lifting chest off pad.
Hold contraction at the top for 1 second.
Lower weight under complete control.
mistakes: Yanking with lower back momentum rather than initiating with active scapular retraction.
Shrugging shoulders into the neck rather than pulling elbows down toward the hip pockets.
formTips: Lie face down on inclined chest support pad with feet hooked securely on platform.

name: Assisted Pull-Up Machine
steps: Select counterweight counter-balance on weight stack.
Kneel or stand on assisted lever platform and grasp pull-up bars with wide grip.
Pull chest up towards bar by driving elbows down to sides.
Pause at peak chin-over-bar position.
Lower body slowly until arms reach full extension.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Select counterweight counter-balance on weight stack.

name: Assisted Dip Machine
steps: Select desired assist weight on machine stack.
Mount platform and grip dip bars with palms facing inward.
Lean slightly forward to bias lower chest fibers.
Lower body until elbows reach 90 degrees.
Press forcefully through palms back to locked out arm position.
mistakes: Descending too deeply with flared elbows, hyperextending anterior shoulder capsules.
Kicking the legs or swinging for momentum instead of clean vertical pressing.
formTips: Select desired assist weight on machine stack.

name: Back Extension Machine
steps: Sit on back extension machine with feet flat on footrest and pad positioned against upper back.
Cross arms across chest or hold handles.
Push back against pad using spinal erectors until spine is in neutral upright alignment.
Hold contraction for 1 second.
Return slowly to forward flexed stretch position.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Sit on back extension machine with feet flat on footrest and pad positioned against upper back.

name: 45-Degree Leg Press
steps: Sit into 45-degree sled press with lower back and hips firmly planted against backrest.
Place feet shoulder-width apart in middle of sled footplate.
Disengage safety locks and lower sled slowly until knees bend to 90 degrees.
Drive forcefully through mid-foot and heels to press sled back up without hyperextending knees.
mistakes: Flaring elbows outward at a 90-degree angle, causing shoulder impingement and anterior rotator cuff stress.
Bouncing the resistance violently off the chest instead of utilizing a controlled eccentric stretch.
Over-arching the lumbar spine and lifting glutes completely off the bench.
formTips: Sit into 45-degree sled press with lower back and hips firmly planted against backrest.

name: Horizontal Leg Press Machine
steps: Sit in seated horizontal leg press machine with back pad adjusted so knees start at 90 degrees.
Place feet flat on footplate shoulder-width apart.
Press platform horizontally away until legs are fully extended.
Pause and slowly return seat sled back to starting stack position.
mistakes: Flaring elbows outward at a 90-degree angle, causing shoulder impingement and anterior rotator cuff stress.
Bouncing the resistance violently off the chest instead of utilizing a controlled eccentric stretch.
Over-arching the lumbar spine and lifting glutes completely off the bench.
formTips: Sit in seated horizontal leg press machine with back pad adjusted so knees start at 90 degrees.

name: Vertical Leg Press Machine
steps: Lie flat on back on floor pad with legs extended directly upward toward vertical carriage.
Place feet shoulder-width flat on platform.
Unlock safeties and lower carriage straight down towards chest with strict control.
Press carriage straight up using quads and glutes.
mistakes: Flaring elbows outward at a 90-degree angle, causing shoulder impingement and anterior rotator cuff stress.
Bouncing the resistance violently off the chest instead of utilizing a controlled eccentric stretch.
Over-arching the lumbar spine and lifting glutes completely off the bench.
formTips: Lie flat on back on floor pad with legs extended directly upward toward vertical carriage.

name: Hack Squat Machine
steps: Position shoulders under padded shoulder rests with back flat against sled pad.
Place feet shoulder-width on platform slightly forward to bias quadriceps.
Release safety levers and squat down until thighs are parallel to footplate.
Drive through mid-foot and heels to return sled to upright starting position.
mistakes: Allowing knees to cave inward (valgus collapse) during the concentric drive phase.
Shifting weight forward onto the toes and lifting heels off the floor.
Rounding the lumbar spine in the hole instead of maintaining rigid abdominal bracing.
formTips: Position shoulders under padded shoulder rests with back flat against sled pad.

name: Smith Machine Squat
steps: Position bar on upper traps across shoulders inside Smith machine frame.
Place feet slightly out in front of hips to maximize knee flexion and quad recruitment.
Rotate bar off safety hooks and descend into deep squat until hips break parallel.
Drive straight up against the guided vertical track.
mistakes: Allowing knees to cave inward (valgus collapse) during the concentric drive phase.
Shifting weight forward onto the toes and lifting heels off the floor.
Rounding the lumbar spine in the hole instead of maintaining rigid abdominal bracing.
formTips: Position bar on upper traps across shoulders inside Smith machine frame.

name: Leg Extension Machine
steps: Adjust back pad so knees align directly with machine pivot axis.
Hook shins behind padded lever arm just above ankles.
Extend legs upward until knees are straight, squeezing rectus femoris hard at peak lockout.
Hold contraction for 1 second.
Lower weights smoothly through 2-3s eccentric return.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Adjust back pad so knees align directly with machine pivot axis.

name: Seated Leg Curl Machine
steps: Adjust thigh hold-down pad tight against quadriceps to prevent hip lift.
Position lower leg pad against Achilles tendon behind ankles.
Curl heels downward and back toward seat squeezing hamstrings hard.
Pause at full flexion.
Slowly extend legs back to starting stretch position.
mistakes: Swinging the torso backward and using hip momentum to throw weights up.
Allowing elbows to drift forward excessively, shifting tension away from the biceps to front delts.
formTips: Adjust thigh hold-down pad tight against quadriceps to prevent hip lift.

name: Lying Leg Curl Machine
steps: Lie face down on contoured bench with knee caps just off bottom of pad.
Position lever pad against lower calves/Achilles tendon.
Grip side handles and curl heels up toward glutes without arching lower back.
Squeeze hamstrings at the top.
Lower weight smoothly under control.
mistakes: Swinging the torso backward and using hip momentum to throw weights up.
Allowing elbows to drift forward excessively, shifting tension away from the biceps to front delts.
formTips: Lie face down on contoured bench with knee caps just off bottom of pad.

name: Standing Leg Curl Machine
steps: Stand facing machine with front of thigh against support pad.
Place back of active ankle against roller pad.
Curl lower leg up toward glute while keeping working hip forward.
Hold peak squeeze for 1 second.
Lower slowly back to straight leg position and switch sides.
mistakes: Swinging the torso backward and using hip momentum to throw weights up.
Allowing elbows to drift forward excessively, shifting tension away from the biceps to front delts.
formTips: Stand facing machine with front of thigh against support pad.

name: Hip Abduction Machine
steps: Sit in machine with pads resting against outer knees and thighs.
Press knees outward against pads spreading legs wide against stack resistance.
Squeeze gluteus medius and minimus hard at full abduction.
Slowly return knees together without letting weight stack touch down.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Sit in machine with pads resting against outer knees and thighs.

name: Hip Adduction Machine
steps: Sit in machine with pads positioned against inner knees and thighs.
Open legs to comfortable wide stretch.
Squeeze inner thighs together driving knees inward until pads touch.
Hold contraction for 1 second.
Control eccentric spread back to start.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Sit in machine with pads positioned against inner knees and thighs.

name: Glute Kickback Machine
steps: Position chest and forearms on support pads with working foot hooked on lever footplate.
Drive foot straight back and up contracting gluteus maximus.
Squeeze glute hard at top of kick.
Return knee slowly forward under control.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Position chest and forearms on support pads with working foot hooked on lever footplate.

name: Plate-Loaded Hip Thrust Machine
steps: Sit into hip thrust machine with upper back on pivot bench and strap/lever secured across hips.
Plant feet flat shoulder-width on platform.
Drive through heels to extend hips fully upward to neutral horizontal lock.
Squeeze glutes hard at the top without hyperextending lumbar spine.
Lower hips back down with controlled cadence.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Sit into hip thrust machine with upper back on pivot bench and strap/lever secured across hips.

name: Seated Calf Raise Machine
steps: Sit on machine with balls of feet on foot bar and thigh pads resting over lower thighs.
Release safety bar and lower heels as far as comfortable for deep soleus stretch.
Drive through balls of feet lifting heels as high as possible into full plantarflexion.
Hold contraction at the top for 1-2 seconds.
Lower slowly back to deep stretch.
mistakes: Using excessive momentum and swinging the torso.
Leading with the hands instead of elbows, engaging the upper traps excessively.
formTips: Sit on machine with balls of feet on foot bar and thigh pads resting over lower thighs.

name: Standing Calf Raise Machine
steps: Stand with balls of feet on step block and shoulder pads resting comfortably across shoulders.
Lower heels below platform level for complete gastrocnemius stretch.
Push forcefully through toes raising body straight up.
Pause at peak calf contraction.
Lower under complete control.
mistakes: Using excessive momentum and swinging the torso.
Leading with the hands instead of elbows, engaging the upper traps excessively.
formTips: Stand with balls of feet on step block and shoulder pads resting comfortably across shoulders.

name: Calf Press on Leg Press Machine
steps: Sit into leg press machine with legs almost fully extended.
Place balls of feet on bottom edge of footplate with heels hanging free.
Press sled forward using ankles only.
Hold peak squeeze for 1 second.
Allow toes to flex backward for deep calf stretch without bending knees.
mistakes: Flaring elbows outward at a 90-degree angle, causing shoulder impingement and anterior rotator cuff stress.
Bouncing the resistance violently off the chest instead of utilizing a controlled eccentric stretch.
Over-arching the lumbar spine and lifting glutes completely off the bench.
formTips: Sit into leg press machine with legs almost fully extended.

name: Preacher Curl Machine
steps: Sit into preacher machine with armpits resting snug at top of preacher pad.
Grip handles with palms facing upward.
Curl handles upward toward shoulders isolating biceps brachii.
Squeeze biceps hard at peak flexion.
Lower handles back down until arms are nearly fully extended.
mistakes: Swinging the torso backward and using hip momentum to throw weights up.
Allowing elbows to drift forward excessively, shifting tension away from the biceps to front delts.
formTips: Sit into preacher machine with armpits resting snug at top of preacher pad.

name: Triceps Extension Machine
steps: Sit with upper arms resting flat on angled support pad.
Grasp handles with neutral or overhand grip.
Extend arms downward pushing handles forward until elbows lock out.
Contract triceps heads intensely at bottom of stroke.
Slowly allow handles to rise back to starting 90-degree elbow bend.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Sit with upper arms resting flat on angled support pad.

name: Triceps Dip Machine
steps: Sit upright with back against pad and grip handles beside hips.
Lock thighs under support roller pads.
Press handles down by extending elbows until arms are straight.
Hold contraction at the bottom for 1 second.
Return slowly to chest height.
mistakes: Descending too deeply with flared elbows, hyperextending anterior shoulder capsules.
Kicking the legs or swinging for momentum instead of clean vertical pressing.
formTips: Sit upright with back against pad and grip handles beside hips.

name: Ab Crunch Machine
steps: Sit in ab machine with feet hooked behind ankle rollers and hands grasping chest/shoulder handles.
Exhale and contract abdominal wall curling torso forward bringing ribs toward pelvis.
Hold peak isometric abdominal contraction for 1-2 seconds.
Slowly return to upright position while inhaling.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Sit in ab machine with feet hooked behind ankle rollers and hands grasping chest/shoulder handles.

name: Torso Rotation Machine
steps: Sit in rotary torso machine with knees hooked securely against thigh pads.
Hold chest handles with spine tall.
Rotate torso smoothly to one side by contracting internal and external obliques.
Pause at peak rotation for 1 second.
Return under control to center and repeat on opposite side.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Sit in rotary torso machine with knees hooked securely against thigh pads.

name: 3/4 Sit-Up
steps: Lie down on the floor and secure your feet. Your legs should be bent at the knees.
Place your hands behind or to the side of your head. You will begin with your back on the ground. This will be your starting position.
Flex your hips and spine to raise your torso toward your knees.
At the top of the contraction your torso should be perpendicular to the ground. Reverse the motion, going only ¾ of the way down.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Lie down on the floor and secure your feet. Your legs should be bent at the knees.

name: 90/90 Hamstring
steps: Lie on your back, with one leg extended straight out.
With the other leg, bend the hip and knee to 90 degrees. You may brace your leg with your hands if necessary. This will be your starting position.
Extend your leg straight into the air, pausing briefly at the top. Return the leg to the starting position.
Repeat for 10-20 repetitions, and then switch to the other leg.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Lie on your back, with one leg extended straight out.

name: Ab Roller
steps: Hold the Ab Roller with both hands and kneel on the floor.
Now place the ab roller on the floor in front of you so that you are on all your hands and knees (as in a kneeling push up position). This will be your starting position.

Slowly roll the ab roller straight forward, stretching your body into a straight position. Tip: Go down as far as you can without touching the floor with your body. Breathe in during this portion of the movement.
After a pause at the stretched position, start pulling yourself back to the starting position as you breathe out. Tip: Go slowly and keep your abs tight at all times.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Hold the Ab Roller with both hands and kneel on the floor.

name: Adductor
steps: Lie face down with one leg on a foam roll.
Rotate the leg so that the foam roll contacts against your inner thigh. Shift as much weight onto the foam roll as can be tolerated.
While trying to relax the muscles if the inner thigh, roll over the foam between your hip and knee, holding points of tension for 10-30 seconds. Repeat with the other leg.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Lie face down with one leg on a foam roll.

name: Adductor/Groin
steps: Lie on your back with your feet raised towards the ceiling.
Have your partner hold your feet or ankles. Abduct your legs as far as you can. This will be your starting position.
Attempt to squeeze your legs together for 10 or more seconds, while your partner prevents you from doing so.

Now, relax the muscles in your legs as your partner pushes your feet apart, stretching as far as is comfortable for you. Be sure to let your partner know when the stretch is adequate to prevent overstretching or injury.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Lie on your back with your feet raised towards the ceiling.

name: Advanced Kettlebell Windmill
steps: Clean and press a kettlebell overhead with one arm.

Keeping the kettlebell locked out at all times, push your butt out in the direction of the locked out kettlebell. Keep the non-working arm behind your back and turn your feet out at a forty-five degree angle from the arm with the kettlebell.
Lower yourself as far as possible.
Pause for a second and reverse the motion back to the starting position.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Clean and press a kettlebell overhead with one arm.

name: Air Bike
steps: Lie flat on the floor with your lower back pressed to the ground. For this exercise, you will need to put your hands beside your head. Be careful however to not strain with the neck as you perform it. Now lift your shoulders into the crunch position.
Bring knees up to where they are perpendicular to the floor, with your lower legs parallel to the floor. This will be your starting position.

Now simultaneously, slowly go through a cycle pedal motion kicking forward with the right leg and bringing in the knee of the left leg. Bring your right elbow close to your left knee by crunching to the side, as you breathe out.
Go back to the initial position as you breathe in.
Crunch to the opposite side as you cycle your legs and bring closer your left elbow to your right knee and exhale.
Continue alternating in this manner until all of the recommended repetitions for each side have been completed.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Lie flat on the floor with your lower back pressed to the ground. For this exercise, you will need to put your hands beside your head. Be careful however to not strain with the neck as you perform it. Now lift your shoulders into the crunch position.

name: All Fours Quad Stretch
steps: Start off on your hands and knees, then lift your leg off the floor and hold the foot with your hand.
Use your hand to hold the foot or ankle, keeping the knee fully flexed, stretching the quadriceps and hip flexors.
Focus on extending your hips, thrusting them towards the floor. Hold for 10-20 seconds and then switch sides.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Start off on your hands and knees, then lift your leg off the floor and hold the foot with your hand.

name: Alternate Hammer Curl
steps: Stand up with your torso upright and a dumbbell in each hand being held at arms length. The elbows should be close to the torso.
The palms of the hands should be facing your torso. This will be your starting position.

While holding the upper arm stationary, curl the right weight forward while contracting the biceps as you breathe out. Continue the movement until your biceps is fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a second as you squeeze the biceps. Tip: Only the forearms should move.
Slowly begin to bring the dumbbells back to starting position as your breathe in.
Repeat the movement with the left hand. This equals one repetition.
Continue alternating in this manner for the recommended amount of repetitions.
mistakes: Swinging the torso backward and using hip momentum to throw weights up.
Allowing elbows to drift forward excessively, shifting tension away from the biceps to front delts.
formTips: Stand up with your torso upright and a dumbbell in each hand being held at arms length. The elbows should be close to the torso.

name: Alternate Heel Touchers
steps: Lie on the floor with the knees bent and the feet on the floor around 18-24 inches apart. Your arms should be extended by your side. This will be your starting position.
Crunch over your torso forward and up about 3-4 inches to the right side and touch your right heel as you hold the contraction for a second. Exhale while performing this movement.
Now go back slowly to the starting position as you inhale.

Now crunch over your torso forward and up around 3-4 inches to the left side and touch your left heel as you hold the contraction for a second. Exhale while performing this movement and then go back to the starting position as you inhale. Now that both heels have been touched, that is considered 1 repetition.
Continue alternating sides in this manner until all prescribed repetitions are done.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Lie on the floor with the knees bent and the feet on the floor around 18-24 inches apart. Your arms should be extended by your side. This will be your starting position.

name: Alternate Incline Dumbbell Curl
steps: Sit down on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand being held at arms length. Tip: Keep the elbows close to the torso.This will be your starting position.

While holding the upper arm stationary, curl the right weight forward while contracting the biceps as you breathe out. As you do so, rotate the hand so that the palm is facing up. Continue the movement until your biceps is fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a second as you squeeze the biceps. Tip: Only the forearms should move.
Slowly begin to bring the dumbbell back to starting position as your breathe in.
Repeat the movement with the left hand. This equals one repetition.
Continue alternating in this manner for the recommended amount of repetitions.
mistakes: Swinging the torso backward and using hip momentum to throw weights up.
Allowing elbows to drift forward excessively, shifting tension away from the biceps to front delts.
formTips: Sit down on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand being held at arms length. Tip: Keep the elbows close to the torso.This will be your starting position.

name: Alternate Leg Diagonal Bound
steps: Assume a comfortable stance with one foot slightly in front of the other.
Begin by pushing off with the front leg, driving the opposite knee forward and as high as possible before landing. Attempt to cover as much distance to each side with each bound.
It may help to use a line on the ground to guage distance from side to side.
Repeat the sequence with the other leg.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Assume a comfortable stance with one foot slightly in front of the other.

name: Alternating Cable Shoulder Press
steps: Move the cables to the bottom of the tower and select an appropriate weight.
Grasp the cables and hold them at shoulder height, palms facing forward. This will be your starting position.
Keeping your head and chest up, extend through the elbow to press one side directly over head.
After pausing at the top, return to the starting position and repeat on the opposite side.
mistakes: Flaring elbows outward at a 90-degree angle, causing shoulder impingement and anterior rotator cuff stress.
Bouncing the resistance violently off the chest instead of utilizing a controlled eccentric stretch.
Over-arching the lumbar spine and lifting glutes completely off the bench.
formTips: Move the cables to the bottom of the tower and select an appropriate weight.

name: Alternating Deltoid Raise
steps: In a standing position, hold a pair of dumbbells at your side.
Keeping your elbows slightly bent, raise the weights directly in front of you to shoulder height, avoiding any swinging or cheating.
Return the weights to your side.
On the next repetition, raise the weights laterally, raising them out to your side to about shoulder height.
Return the weights to the starting position and continue alternating to the front and side.
mistakes: Using excessive momentum and swinging the torso.
Leading with the hands instead of elbows, engaging the upper traps excessively.
formTips: In a standing position, hold a pair of dumbbells at your side.

name: Alternating Floor Press
steps: Lie on the floor with two kettlebells next to your shoulders.
Position one in place on your chest and then the other, gripping the kettlebells on the handle with the palms facing forward.
Extend both arms, so that the kettlebells are being held above your chest. Lower one kettlebell, bringing it to your chest and turn the wrist in the direction of the locked out kettlebell.
Raise the kettlebell and repeat on the opposite side.
mistakes: Flaring elbows outward at a 90-degree angle, causing shoulder impingement and anterior rotator cuff stress.
Bouncing the resistance violently off the chest instead of utilizing a controlled eccentric stretch.
Over-arching the lumbar spine and lifting glutes completely off the bench.
formTips: Lie on the floor with two kettlebells next to your shoulders.

name: Alternating Hang Clean
steps: Place two kettlebells between your feet. To get in the starting position, push your butt back and look straight ahead.

Clean one kettlebell to your shoulder and hold on to the other kettlebell in a hanging position. Clean the kettlebell to your shoulder by extending through the legs and hips as you pull the kettlebell towards your shoulders. Rotate your wrist as you do so.
Lower the cleaned kettlebell to a hanging position and clean the alternate kettlebell. Repeat.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Place two kettlebells between your feet. To get in the starting position, push your butt back and look straight ahead.

name: Alternating Kettlebell Press
steps: Clean two kettlebells to your shoulders. Clean the kettlebells to your shoulders by extending through the legs and hips as you pull the kettlebells towards your shoulders. Rotate your wrists as you do so.
Press one directly overhead by extending through the elbow, turning it so the palm faces forward while holding the other kettlebell stationary .
Lower the pressed kettlebell to the starting position and immediately press with your other arm.
mistakes: Flaring elbows outward at a 90-degree angle, causing shoulder impingement and anterior rotator cuff stress.
Bouncing the resistance violently off the chest instead of utilizing a controlled eccentric stretch.
Over-arching the lumbar spine and lifting glutes completely off the bench.
formTips: Clean two kettlebells to your shoulders. Clean the kettlebells to your shoulders by extending through the legs and hips as you pull the kettlebells towards your shoulders. Rotate your wrists as you do so.

name: Alternating Kettlebell Row
steps: Place two kettlebells in front of your feet. Bend your knees slightly and push your butt out as much as possible. As you bend over to get into the starting position grab both kettlebells by the handles.

Pull one kettlebell off of the floor while holding on to the other kettlebell. Retract the shoulder blade of the working side, as you flex the elbow, drawing the kettlebell towards your stomach or rib cage.
Lower the kettlebell in the working arm and repeat with your other arm.
mistakes: Yanking with lower back momentum rather than initiating with active scapular retraction.
Shrugging shoulders into the neck rather than pulling elbows down toward the hip pockets.
formTips: Place two kettlebells in front of your feet. Bend your knees slightly and push your butt out as much as possible. As you bend over to get into the starting position grab both kettlebells by the handles.

name: Alternating Renegade Row
steps: Place two kettlebells on the floor about shoulder width apart. Position yourself on your toes and your hands as though you were doing a pushup, with the body straight and extended. Use the handles of the kettlebells to support your upper body. You may need to position your feet wide for support.
Push one kettlebell into the floor and row the other kettlebell, retracting the shoulder blade of the working side as you flex the elbow, pulling it to your side.
Then lower the kettlebell to the floor and begin the kettlebell in the opposite hand. Repeat for several reps.
mistakes: Yanking with lower back momentum rather than initiating with active scapular retraction.
Shrugging shoulders into the neck rather than pulling elbows down toward the hip pockets.
formTips: Place two kettlebells on the floor about shoulder width apart. Position yourself on your toes and your hands as though you were doing a pushup, with the body straight and extended. Use the handles of the kettlebells to support your upper body. You may need to position your feet wide for support.

name: Ankle Circles
steps: Use a sturdy object like a squat rack to hold yourself.

Lift the right leg in the air (just around 2 inches from the floor) and perform a circular motion with the big toe. Pretend that you are drawing a big circle with it. Tip: One circle equals 1 repetition. Breathe normally as you perform the movement.
When you are done with the right foot, then repeat with the left leg.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Use a sturdy object like a squat rack to hold yourself.

name: Ankle On The Knee
steps: From a lying position, bend your knees and keep your feet on the floor.
Place your ankle of one foot on your opposite knee.
Grasp the thigh or knee of the bottom leg and pull both of your legs into the chest. Relax your neck and shoulders. Hold for 10-20 seconds and then switch sides.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: From a lying position, bend your knees and keep your feet on the floor.

name: Anterior Tibialis-SMR
steps: Begin seated on the ground with your legs bent and your feet on the floor.

Using a Muscle Roller or a rolling pin, apply pressure to the muscles on the outside of your shins. Work from just below the knee to above the ankle, pausing at points of tension for 10-30 seconds. Repeat on the other leg.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Begin seated on the ground with your legs bent and your feet on the floor.

name: Anti-Gravity Press
steps: Place a bar on the ground behind the head of an incline bench.
Lay on the bench face down. With a pronated grip, pick the barbell up from the floor. Flex the elbows, performing a reverse curl to bring the bar near your chest. This will be your starting position.
To begin, press the barbell out in front of your head by extending your elbows. Keep your arms parallel to the ground throughout the movement.
Return to the starting position and repeat to complete the set.
mistakes: Flaring elbows outward at a 90-degree angle, causing shoulder impingement and anterior rotator cuff stress.
Bouncing the resistance violently off the chest instead of utilizing a controlled eccentric stretch.
Over-arching the lumbar spine and lifting glutes completely off the bench.
formTips: Place a bar on the ground behind the head of an incline bench.

name: Arm Circles
steps: Stand up and extend your arms straight out by the sides. The arms should be parallel to the floor and perpendicular (90-degree angle) to your torso. This will be your starting position.
Slowly start to make circles of about 1 foot in diameter with each outstretched arm. Breathe normally as you perform the movement.
Continue the circular motion of the outstretched arms for about ten seconds. Then reverse the movement, going the opposite direction.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Stand up and extend your arms straight out by the sides. The arms should be parallel to the floor and perpendicular (90-degree angle) to your torso. This will be your starting position.

name: Arnold Dumbbell Press
steps: Sit on an exercise bench with back support and hold two dumbbells in front of you at about upper chest level with your palms facing your body and your elbows bent. Tip: Your arms should be next to your torso. The starting position should look like the contracted portion of a dumbbell curl.
Now to perform the movement, raise the dumbbells as you rotate the palms of your hands until they are facing forward.
Continue lifting the dumbbells until your arms are extended above you in straight arm position. Breathe out as you perform this portion of the movement.

After a second pause at the top, begin to lower the dumbbells to the original position by rotating the palms of your hands towards you. Tip: The left arm will be rotated in a counter clockwise manner while the right one will be rotated clockwise. Breathe in as you perform this portion of the movement.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
mistakes: Flaring elbows outward at a 90-degree angle, causing shoulder impingement and anterior rotator cuff stress.
Bouncing the resistance violently off the chest instead of utilizing a controlled eccentric stretch.
Over-arching the lumbar spine and lifting glutes completely off the bench.
formTips: Sit on an exercise bench with back support and hold two dumbbells in front of you at about upper chest level with your palms facing your body and your elbows bent. Tip: Your arms should be next to your torso. The starting position should look like the contracted portion of a dumbbell curl.

name: Around The Worlds
steps: Lay down on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in each hand with the palms of the hands facing towards the ceiling. Tip: Your arms should be parallel to the floor and next to your thighs. To avoid injury, make sure that you keep your elbows slightly bent. This will be your starting position.

Now move the dumbbells by creating a semi-circle as you displace them from the initial position to over the head. All of the movement should happen with the arms parallel to the floor at all times. Breathe in as you perform this portion of the movement.
Reverse the movement to return the weight to the starting position as you exhale.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Lay down on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in each hand with the palms of the hands facing towards the ceiling. Tip: Your arms should be parallel to the floor and next to your thighs. To avoid injury, make sure that you keep your elbows slightly bent. This will be your starting position.

name: Atlas Stone Trainer
steps: This trainer is effective for developing Atlas Stone strength for those who don't have access to stones, and are typically made from bar ends or heavy pipe.
Begin by loading the desired weight onto the bar. Straddle the weight, wrapping your arms around the implement, bending at the hips.

Begin by pulling the weight up past the knees, extending through the hips. As the weight clears the knees, it can be lapped by resting it on your thighs and sitting back, hugging it tightly to your chest.
Finish the movement by extending through your hips and knees to raise the weight as high as possible. The weight can be returned to the lap or to the ground for successive repetitions.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: This trainer is effective for developing Atlas Stone strength for those who don't have access to stones, and are typically made from bar ends or heavy pipe.

name: Atlas Stones
steps: Begin with the atlas stone between your feet. Bend at the hips to wrap your arms vertically around the Atlas Stone, attempting to get your fingers underneath the stone. Many stones will have a small flat portion on the bottom, which will make the stone easier to hold.
Pulling the stone into your torso, drive through the back half of your feet to pull the stone from the ground.
As the stone passes the knees, lap it by sitting backward, pulling the stone on top of your thighs.

Sit low, getting the stone high onto your chest as you change your grip to reach over the stone. Stand, driving through with your hips. Close distance to the loading platform, and lean back, extending the hips to get the stone as high as possible.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Begin with the atlas stone between your feet. Bend at the hips to wrap your arms vertically around the Atlas Stone, attempting to get your fingers underneath the stone. Many stones will have a small flat portion on the bottom, which will make the stone easier to hold.

name: Axle Deadlift
steps: Approach the bar so that it is centered over your feet. You feet should be about hip width apart. Bend at the hip to grip the bar at shoulder width, allowing your shoulder blades to protract. Typically, you would use an over/under grip.

With your feet and your grip set, take a big breath and then lower your hips and flex the knees until your shins contact the bar. Look forward with your head, keep your chest up and your back arched, and begin driving through the heels to move the weight upward.
After the bar passes the knees, aggressively pull the bar back, pulling your shoulder blades together as you drive your hips forward into the bar.
Lower the bar by bending at the hips and guiding it to the floor.
mistakes: Rounding the lumbar spine when breaking the bar off the floor.
Letting the barbell drift away from the shins, drastically lengthening the moment arm.
Hyperextending the spine at lockout instead of squeezing the glutes.
formTips: Approach the bar so that it is centered over your feet. You feet should be about hip width apart. Bend at the hip to grip the bar at shoulder width, allowing your shoulder blades to protract. Typically, you would use an over/under grip.

name: Back Flyes - With Bands
steps: Run a band around a stationary post like that of a squat rack.
Grab the band by the handles and stand back so that the tension in the band rises.

Extend and lift the arms straight in front of you. Tip: Your arms should be straight and parallel to the floor while perpendicular to your torso. Your feet should be firmly planted on the floor spread at shoulder width. This will be your starting position.
As you exhale, move your arms to the sides and back. Keep your arms extended and parallel to the floor. Continue the movement until the arms are extended to your sides.
After a pause, go back to the original position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Run a band around a stationary post like that of a squat rack.

name: Backward Drag
steps: Load a sled with the desired weight, attaching a rope or straps to the sled that you can hold onto.
Begin the exercise by moving backwards for a given distance. Leaning back, extend through the legs for short steps to move as quickly as possible.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Load a sled with the desired weight, attaching a rope or straps to the sled that you can hold onto.

name: Backward Medicine Ball Throw
steps: This exercise is best done with a partner. If you lack a partner, the ball can be thrown and retrieved or thrown against a wall.
Begin standing a few meters in front of your partner, both facing the same direction. Begin holding the ball between your legs.
Squat down and then forcefully reverse direction, coming to full extension and you toss the ball over your head to your partner.
Your partner can then roll the ball back to you. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Yanking with lower back momentum rather than initiating with active scapular retraction.
Shrugging shoulders into the neck rather than pulling elbows down toward the hip pockets.
formTips: This exercise is best done with a partner. If you lack a partner, the ball can be thrown and retrieved or thrown against a wall.

name: Balance Board
steps: Place a balance board in front of you.
Stand up on it and try to balance yourself.
Hold the balance for as long as desired.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Place a balance board in front of you.

name: Ball Leg Curl
steps: Begin on the floor laying on your back with your feet on top of the ball.
Position the ball so that when your legs are extended your ankles are on top of the ball. This will be your starting position.
Raise your hips off of the ground, keeping your weight on the shoulder blades and your feet.
Flex the knees, pulling the ball as close to you as you can, contracting the hamstrings.
After a brief pause, return to the starting position.
mistakes: Swinging the torso backward and using hip momentum to throw weights up.
Allowing elbows to drift forward excessively, shifting tension away from the biceps to front delts.
formTips: Begin on the floor laying on your back with your feet on top of the ball.

name: Band Assisted Pull-Up
steps: Choke the band around the center of the pullup bar. You can use different bands to provide varying levels of assistance.
Pull the end of the band down, and place one bent knee into the loop, ensuring it won't slip out. Take a medium to wide grip on the bar. This will be your starting position.

Pull yourself upward by contracting the lats as you flex the elbow. The elbow should be driven to your side. Pull to the front, attempting to get your chin over the bar. Avoid swinging or jerking movements.
After a brief pause, return to the starting position.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Choke the band around the center of the pullup bar. You can use different bands to provide varying levels of assistance.

name: Band Good Morning
steps: Using a 41 inch band, stand on one end, spreading your feet a small amount. Bend at the hips to loop the end of the band behind your neck. This will be your starting position.
Keeping your legs straight, extend through the hips to come to a near vertical position.
Ensure that you do not round your back as you go down back to the starting position.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Using a 41 inch band, stand on one end, spreading your feet a small amount. Bend at the hips to loop the end of the band behind your neck. This will be your starting position.

name: Band Good Morning (Pull Through)
steps: Loop the band around a post. Standing a little ways away, loop the opposite end around the neck. Your hands can help hold the band in position.
Begin by bending at the hips, getting your butt back as far as possible. Keep your back flat and bend forward to about 90 degrees. Your knees should be only slightly bent.
Return to the starting position be driving through with the hips to come back to a standing position.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Loop the band around a post. Standing a little ways away, loop the opposite end around the neck. Your hands can help hold the band in position.

name: Band Hip Adductions
steps: Anchor a band around a solid post or other object.
Stand with your left side to the post, and put your right foot through the band, getting it around the ankle.
Stand up straight and hold onto the post if needed. This will be your starting position.
Keeping the knee straight, raise your right legs out to the side as far as you can.
Return to the starting position and repeat for the desired rep count.
Switch sides.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Anchor a band around a solid post or other object.

name: Band Pull Apart
steps: Begin with your arms extended straight out in front of you, holding the band with both hands.
Initiate the movement by performing a reverse fly motion, moving your hands out laterally to your sides.
Keep your elbows extended as you perform the movement, bringing the band to your chest. Ensure that you keep your shoulders back during the exercise.
Pause as you complete the movement, returning to the starting position under control.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Begin with your arms extended straight out in front of you, holding the band with both hands.

name: Band Skull Crusher
steps: Secure a band to the base of a rack or the bench. Lay on the bench so that the band is lined up with your head.
Take hold of the band, raising your elbows so that the upper arm is perpendicular to the floor. With the elbow flexed, the band should be above your head. This will be your starting position.
Extend through the elbow to straighten your arm, keeping your upper arm in place. Pause at the top of the motion, and return to the starting position.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Secure a band to the base of a rack or the bench. Lay on the bench so that the band is lined up with your head.

name: Barbell Ab Rollout
steps: For this exercise you will need to get into a pushup position, but instead of having your hands of the floor, you will be grabbing on to an Olympic barbell (loaded with 5-10 lbs on each side) instead. This will be your starting position.

While keeping a slight arch on your back, lift your hips and roll the barbell towards your feet as you exhale. Tip: As you perform the movement, your glutes should be coming up, you should be keeping the abs tight and should maintain your back posture at all times. Also your arms should be staying perpendicular to the floor throughout the movement. If you don't, you will work out your shoulders and back more than the abs.
After a second contraction at the top, start to roll the barbell back forward to the starting position slowly as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: For this exercise you will need to get into a pushup position, but instead of having your hands of the floor, you will be grabbing on to an Olympic barbell (loaded with 5-10 lbs on each side) instead. This will be your starting position.

name: Barbell Ab Rollout - On Knees
steps: Hold an Olympic barbell loaded with 5-10lbs on each side and kneel on the floor.
Now place the barbell on the floor in front of you so that you are on all your hands and knees (as in a kneeling push up position). This will be your starting position.

Slowly roll the barbell straight forward, stretching your body into a straight position. Tip: Go down as far as you can without touching the floor with your body. Breathe in during this portion of the movement.
After a second pause at the stretched position, start pulling yourself back to the starting position as you breathe out. Tip: Go slowly and keep your abs tight at all times.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Hold an Olympic barbell loaded with 5-10lbs on each side and kneel on the floor.

name: Barbell Bench Press - Medium Grip
steps: Lie back on a flat bench. Using a medium width grip (a grip that creates a 90-degree angle in the middle of the movement between the forearms and the upper arms), lift the bar from the rack and hold it straight over you with your arms locked. This will be your starting position.
From the starting position, breathe in and begin coming down slowly until the bar touches your middle chest.

After a brief pause, push the bar back to the starting position as you breathe out. Focus on pushing the bar using your chest muscles. Lock your arms and squeeze your chest in the contracted position at the top of the motion, hold for a second and then start coming down slowly again. Tip: Ideally, lowering the weight should take about twice as long as raising it.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
When you are done, place the bar back in the rack.
mistakes: Flaring elbows outward at a 90-degree angle, causing shoulder impingement and anterior rotator cuff stress.
Bouncing the resistance violently off the chest instead of utilizing a controlled eccentric stretch.
Over-arching the lumbar spine and lifting glutes completely off the bench.
formTips: Lie back on a flat bench. Using a medium width grip (a grip that creates a 90-degree angle in the middle of the movement between the forearms and the upper arms), lift the bar from the rack and hold it straight over you with your arms locked. This will be your starting position.

name: Barbell Curl
steps: Stand up with your torso upright while holding a barbell at a shoulder-width grip. The palm of your hands should be facing forward and the elbows should be close to the torso. This will be your starting position.
While holding the upper arms stationary, curl the weights forward while contracting the biceps as you breathe out. Tip: Only the forearms should move.
Continue the movement until your biceps are fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a second and squeeze the biceps hard.
Slowly begin to bring the bar back to starting position as your breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
mistakes: Swinging the torso backward and using hip momentum to throw weights up.
Allowing elbows to drift forward excessively, shifting tension away from the biceps to front delts.
formTips: Stand up with your torso upright while holding a barbell at a shoulder-width grip. The palm of your hands should be facing forward and the elbows should be close to the torso. This will be your starting position.

name: Barbell Curls Lying Against An Incline
steps: Lie against an incline bench, with your arms holding a barbell and hanging down in a horizontal line. This will be your starting position.

While keeping the upper arms stationary, curl the weight up as high as you can while squeezing the biceps. Breathe out as you perform this portion of the movement. Tip: Only the forearms should move. Do not swing the arms.
After a second contraction, slowly go back to the starting position as you inhale. Tip: Make sure that you go all of the way down.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
mistakes: Swinging the torso backward and using hip momentum to throw weights up.
Allowing elbows to drift forward excessively, shifting tension away from the biceps to front delts.
formTips: Lie against an incline bench, with your arms holding a barbell and hanging down in a horizontal line. This will be your starting position.

name: Barbell Deadlift
steps: Stand in front of a loaded barbell.

While keeping the back as straight as possible, bend your knees, bend forward and grasp the bar using a medium (shoulder width) overhand grip. This will be the starting position of the exercise. Tip: If it is difficult to hold on to the bar with this grip, alternate your grip or use wrist straps.

While holding the bar, start the lift by pushing with your legs while simultaneously getting your torso to the upright position as you breathe out. In the upright position, stick your chest out and contract the back by bringing the shoulder blades back. Think of how the soldiers in the military look when they are in standing in attention.

Go back to the starting position by bending at the knees while simultaneously leaning the torso forward at the waist while keeping the back straight. When the weights on the bar touch the floor you are back at the starting position and ready to perform another repetition.
Perform the amount of repetitions prescribed in the program.
mistakes: Rounding the lumbar spine when breaking the bar off the floor.
Letting the barbell drift away from the shins, drastically lengthening the moment arm.
Hyperextending the spine at lockout instead of squeezing the glutes.
formTips: Stand in front of a loaded barbell.

name: Barbell Full Squat
steps: This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for safety purposes. To begin, first set the bar on a rack just above shoulder level. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, step under the bar and place the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck) across it.
Hold on to the bar using both arms at each side and lift it off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straightening your torso.

Step away from the rack and position your legs using a shoulder-width medium stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up at all times and maintain a straight back. This will be your starting position.

Begin to slowly lower the bar by bending the knees and sitting back with your hips as you maintain a straight posture with the head up. Continue down until your hamstrings are on your calves. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement.
Begin to raise the bar as you exhale by pushing the floor with the heel or middle of your foot as you straighten the legs and extend the hips to go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
mistakes: Allowing knees to cave inward (valgus collapse) during the concentric drive phase.
Shifting weight forward onto the toes and lifting heels off the floor.
Rounding the lumbar spine in the hole instead of maintaining rigid abdominal bracing.
formTips: This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for safety purposes. To begin, first set the bar on a rack just above shoulder level. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, step under the bar and place the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck) across it.

name: Barbell Glute Bridge
steps: Begin seated on the ground with a loaded barbell over your legs. Using a fat bar or having a pad on the bar can greatly reduce the discomfort caused by this exercise. Roll the bar so that it is directly above your hips, and lay down flat on the floor.
Begin the movement by driving through with your heels, extending your hips vertically through the bar. Your weight should be supported by your upper back and the heels of your feet.
Extend as far as possible, then reverse the motion to return to the starting position.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Begin seated on the ground with a loaded barbell over your legs. Using a fat bar or having a pad on the bar can greatly reduce the discomfort caused by this exercise. Roll the bar so that it is directly above your hips, and lay down flat on the floor.

name: Barbell Guillotine Bench Press
steps: Using a medium width grip (a grip that creates a 90-degree angle in the middle of the movement between the forearms and the upper arms), lift the bar from the rack and hold it straight over your neck with your arms locked. This will be your starting position.
As you breathe in, bring the bar down slowly until it is about 1 inch from your neck.

After a second pause, bring the bar back to the starting position as you breathe out and push the bar using your chest muscles. Lock your arms and squeeze your chest in the contracted position, hold for a second and then start coming down slowly again. It should take at least twice as long to go down than to come up.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
When you are done, place the bar back in the rack.
mistakes: Flaring elbows outward at a 90-degree angle, causing shoulder impingement and anterior rotator cuff stress.
Bouncing the resistance violently off the chest instead of utilizing a controlled eccentric stretch.
Over-arching the lumbar spine and lifting glutes completely off the bench.
formTips: Using a medium width grip (a grip that creates a 90-degree angle in the middle of the movement between the forearms and the upper arms), lift the bar from the rack and hold it straight over your neck with your arms locked. This will be your starting position.

name: Barbell Hack Squat
steps: Stand up straight while holding a barbell behind you at arms length and your feet at shoulder width. Tip: A shoulder width grip is best with the palms of your hands facing back. You can use wrist wraps for this exercise for a better grip. This will be your starting position.
While keeping your head and eyes up and back straight, squat until your upper thighs are parallel to the floor. Breathe in as you slowly go down.
Pressing mainly with the heel of the foot and squeezing the thighs, go back up as you breathe out.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
mistakes: Allowing knees to cave inward (valgus collapse) during the concentric drive phase.
Shifting weight forward onto the toes and lifting heels off the floor.
Rounding the lumbar spine in the hole instead of maintaining rigid abdominal bracing.
formTips: Stand up straight while holding a barbell behind you at arms length and your feet at shoulder width. Tip: A shoulder width grip is best with the palms of your hands facing back. You can use wrist wraps for this exercise for a better grip. This will be your starting position.

name: Barbell Hip Thrust
steps: Begin seated on the ground with a bench directly behind you. Have a loaded barbell over your legs. Using a fat bar or having a pad on the bar can greatly reduce the discomfort caused by this exercise.
Roll the bar so that it is directly above your hips, and lean back against the bench so that your shoulder blades are near the top of it.

Begin the movement by driving through your feet, extending your hips vertically through the bar. Your weight should be supported by your shoulder blades and your feet. Extend as far as possible, then reverse the motion to return to the starting position.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Begin seated on the ground with a bench directly behind you. Have a loaded barbell over your legs. Using a fat bar or having a pad on the bar can greatly reduce the discomfort caused by this exercise.

name: Barbell Incline Bench Press - Medium Grip
steps: Lie back on an incline bench. Using a medium-width grip (a grip that creates a 90-degree angle in the middle of the movement between the forearms and the upper arms), lift the bar from the rack and hold it straight over you with your arms locked. This will be your starting position.
As you breathe in, come down slowly until you feel the bar on you upper chest.

After a second pause, bring the bar back to the starting position as you breathe out and push the bar using your chest muscles. Lock your arms in the contracted position, squeeze your chest, hold for a second and then start coming down slowly again. Tip: it should take at least twice as long to go down than to come up.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
When you are done, place the bar back in the rack.
mistakes: Flaring elbows outward at a 90-degree angle, causing shoulder impingement and anterior rotator cuff stress.
Bouncing the resistance violently off the chest instead of utilizing a controlled eccentric stretch.
Over-arching the lumbar spine and lifting glutes completely off the bench.
formTips: Lie back on an incline bench. Using a medium-width grip (a grip that creates a 90-degree angle in the middle of the movement between the forearms and the upper arms), lift the bar from the rack and hold it straight over you with your arms locked. This will be your starting position.

name: Barbell Incline Shoulder Raise
steps: Lie back on an Incline Bench. Using a medium width grip (a grip that is slightly wider than shoulder width), lift the bar from the rack and hold it straight over you with your arms straight. This will be your starting position.
While keeping the arms straight, lift the bar by protracting your shoulder blades, raising the shoulders from the bench as you breathe out.
Bring back the bar to the starting position as you breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
mistakes: Using excessive momentum and swinging the torso.
Leading with the hands instead of elbows, engaging the upper traps excessively.
formTips: Lie back on an Incline Bench. Using a medium width grip (a grip that is slightly wider than shoulder width), lift the bar from the rack and hold it straight over you with your arms straight. This will be your starting position.

name: Barbell Lunge
steps: This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for safety purposes. To begin, first set the bar on a rack just below shoulder level. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, step under the bar and place the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck) across it.
Hold on to the bar using both arms at each side and lift it off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straightening your torso.

Step away from the rack and step forward with your right leg and squat down through your hips, while keeping the torso upright and maintaining balance. Inhale as you go down. Note: Do not allow your knee to go forward beyond your toes as you come down, as this will put undue stress on the knee joint. li>
Using mainly the heel of your foot, push up and go back to the starting position as you exhale.
Repeat the movement for the recommended amount of repetitions and then perform with the left leg.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for safety purposes. To begin, first set the bar on a rack just below shoulder level. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, step under the bar and place the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck) across it.

name: Barbell Rear Delt Row
steps: Stand up straight while holding a barbell using a wide (higher than shoulder width) and overhand (palms facing your body) grip.

Bend knees slightly and bend over as you keep the natural arch of your back. Let the arms hang in front of you as they hold the bar. Once your torso is parallel to the floor, flare the elbows out and away from your body. Tip: Your torso and your arms should resemble the letter "T". Now you are ready to begin the exercise.

While keeping the upper arms perpendicular to the torso, pull the barbell up towards your upper chest as you squeeze the rear delts and you breathe out. Tip: When performed correctly, this exercise should resemble a bench press in reverse. Also, refrain from using your biceps to do the work. Focus on targeting the rear delts; the arms should only act as hooks.
Slowly go back to the initial position as you breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
mistakes: Yanking with lower back momentum rather than initiating with active scapular retraction.
Shrugging shoulders into the neck rather than pulling elbows down toward the hip pockets.
formTips: Stand up straight while holding a barbell using a wide (higher than shoulder width) and overhand (palms facing your body) grip.

name: Barbell Rollout from Bench
steps: Place a loaded barbell on the ground, near the end of a bench. Kneel with both legs on the bench, and take a medium to narrow grip on the barbell. This will be your starting position.
To begin, extend through the hips to slowly roll the bar forward. As you roll out, flex the shoulder to roll the bar above your head. Ensure that your arms remain extended throughout the movement.
When the bar has been moved as far forward as possible, return to the starting position.
mistakes: Flaring elbows outward at a 90-degree angle, causing shoulder impingement and anterior rotator cuff stress.
Bouncing the resistance violently off the chest instead of utilizing a controlled eccentric stretch.
Over-arching the lumbar spine and lifting glutes completely off the bench.
formTips: Place a loaded barbell on the ground, near the end of a bench. Kneel with both legs on the bench, and take a medium to narrow grip on the barbell. This will be your starting position.

name: Barbell Seated Calf Raise
steps: Place a block about 12 inches in front of a flat bench.
Sit on the bench and place the ball of your feet on the block.
Have someone place a barbell over your upper thighs about 3 inches above your knees and hold it there. This will be your starting position.
Raise up on your toes as high as possible as you squeeze the calves and as you breathe out.
After a second contraction, slowly go back to the starting position. Tip: To get maximum benefit stretch your calves as far as you can.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
mistakes: Using excessive momentum and swinging the torso.
Leading with the hands instead of elbows, engaging the upper traps excessively.
formTips: Place a block about 12 inches in front of a flat bench.

name: Barbell Shoulder Press
steps: Sit on a bench with back support in a squat rack. Position a barbell at a height that is just above your head. Grab the barbell with a pronated grip (palms facing forward).

Once you pick up the barbell with the correct grip width, lift the bar up over your head by locking your arms. Hold at about shoulder level and slightly in front of your head. This is your starting position.
Lower the bar down to the shoulders slowly as you inhale.
Lift the bar back up to the starting position as you exhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
mistakes: Flaring elbows outward at a 90-degree angle, causing shoulder impingement and anterior rotator cuff stress.
Bouncing the resistance violently off the chest instead of utilizing a controlled eccentric stretch.
Over-arching the lumbar spine and lifting glutes completely off the bench.
formTips: Sit on a bench with back support in a squat rack. Position a barbell at a height that is just above your head. Grab the barbell with a pronated grip (palms facing forward).

name: Barbell Shrug
steps: Stand up straight with your feet at shoulder width as you hold a barbell with both hands in front of you using a pronated grip (palms facing the thighs). Tip: Your hands should be a little wider than shoulder width apart. You can use wrist wraps for this exercise for a better grip. This will be your starting position.
Raise your shoulders up as far as you can go as you breathe out and hold the contraction for a second. Tip: Refrain from trying to lift the barbell by using your biceps.
Slowly return to the starting position as you breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Stand up straight with your feet at shoulder width as you hold a barbell with both hands in front of you using a pronated grip (palms facing the thighs). Tip: Your hands should be a little wider than shoulder width apart. You can use wrist wraps for this exercise for a better grip. This will be your starting position.

name: Barbell Shrug Behind The Back
steps: Stand up straight with your feet at shoulder width as you hold a barbell with both hands behind your back using a pronated grip (palms facing back). Tip: Your hands should be a little wider than shoulder width apart. You can use wrist wraps for this exercise for better grip. This will be your starting position.

Raise your shoulders up as far as you can go as you breathe out and hold the contraction for a second. Tip: Refrain from trying to lift the barbell by using your biceps. The arms should remain stretched out at all times.
Slowly return to the starting position as you breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
Failing to brace core and breathing erratically during execution.
formTips: Stand up straight with your feet at shoulder width as you hold a barbell with both hands behind your back using a pronated grip (palms facing back). Tip: Your hands should be a little wider than shoulder width apart. You can use wrist wraps for this exercise for better grip. This will be your starting position.

name: Barbell Side Bend
steps: Stand up straight while holding a barbell placed on the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck). Your feet should be shoulder width apart. This will be your starting position.

While keeping your back straight and your head up, bend only at the waist to the right as far as possible. Breathe in as you bend to the side. Then hold for a second and come back up to the starting position as you exhale. Tip: Keep the rest of the body stationary.
Now repeat the movement but bending to the left instead. Hold for a second and come back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
mistakes: Rushing through repetitions without a controlled 2-3 second eccentric tempo.
