name: Seated Straight Leg Calf Stretch
formTips: Reach out with your hands and try to touch your toes, keeping your legs straight.
steps: Reach out with your hands and try to touch your toes, keeping your legs straight.
If you can't reach your toes, use a towel or resistance band by placing it around the balls of your feet and holding each end.
Pull gently on the towel or band, drawing your toes towards your body, until you feel a stretch in your calves.
Hold this position for about 30 seconds, then release and repeat for several rounds.
mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: Standing Arms Circling
formTips: Start to slowly make circles with your arms, keeping them straight at all times.
steps: Start to slowly make circles with your arms, keeping them straight at all times.
Start with small circles and gradually increase the size of the circles.
After doing this for about 30 seconds, reverse the direction of your circles.
Continue this exercise for a desired amount of time or repetitions, then slowly lower your arms to your sides to finish.
mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: V-up
formTips: Engage your core and at the same time, lift your legs and upper body off the floor to form a V shape.
steps: Engage your core and at the same time, lift your legs and upper body off the floor to form a V shape.
Reach your hands toward your feet, keeping your legs and arms as straight as possible.
Hold this position for a moment, then slowly lower your arms and legs back to the starting position.
Repeat the exercise for your desired number of reps, ensuring to keep your movements controlled and your core engaged throughout.
mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: Cable Seated Neck Flexion
formTips: Sit on the bench of the cable machine, facing away from the pulley, and place the rope handle behind your head, holding each end with your hands.
steps: Sit on the bench of the cable machine, facing away from the pulley, and place the rope handle behind your head, holding each end with your hands.
With your back straight and your eyes looking forward, slowly flex your neck forward, bringing your chin towards your chest while resisting the pull of the cable.
Pause for a moment when your chin is near your chest, then slowly return to the starting position, maintaining control and resisting the pull of the cable.
Repeat this motion for the desired number of repetitions, making sure to keep your movements slow and controlled throughout the exercise.
mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: Dumbbell Jumping Squat
formTips: Lower your body into a squat position by bending your knees and pushing your hips back, keeping your chest upright and your knees over your toes.
steps: Lower your body into a squat position by bending your knees and pushing your hips back, keeping your chest upright and your knees over your toes.
Once you're in a deep squat, push through your heels to jump up explosively, swinging the dumbbells upward to shoulder height as you rise.
As you land, control your body back into the squat position, absorbing the impact with your legs, and immediately prepare for the next jump.
Repeat this process for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining a smooth and controlled rhythm throughout the exercise.
mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: Dip on Floor with Chair
formTips: Bend your knees to sit down and place your hands on the edge of the chair, fingers pointing towards your body.
steps: Bend your knees to sit down and place your hands on the edge of the chair, fingers pointing towards your body.
Push off your hands and slide your bottom off the chair, lowering your body towards the floor by bending your elbows until they are at about a 90-degree angle.
Push your body back up using your arms until they are fully extended, ensuring your hips are close to the chair and your chest is lifted.
Repeat this process for your desired number of repetitions, ensuring to maintain proper form throughout the exercise.
mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: Jumping Jack
formTips: In one swift motion, jump your feet out to the sides and raise your arms above your head.
steps: In one swift motion, jump your feet out to the sides and raise your arms above your head.
Quickly reverse the movement, jumping back to your starting position with your feet together and arms at your sides.
Repeat this action continuously for a set amount of time or repetitions.
Remember to keep your posture straight and maintain a steady rhythm throughout the exercise.
mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: Front and Back Neck Stretch
formTips: For the front neck stretch, slowly tilt your head back until you're looking at the ceiling, feeling a stretch in the front part of your neck; hold this position for 15-30 seconds.
steps: For the front neck stretch, slowly tilt your head back until you're looking at the ceiling, feeling a stretch in the front part of your neck; hold this position for 15-30 seconds.
Gently return your head to the neutral position, looking straight forward.
For the back neck stretch, slowly lower your chin towards your chest, feeling a stretch in the back part of your neck; hold this position for 15-30 seconds.
Slowly lift your head back to the neutral position, and repeat these steps as needed, ensuring to keep movements smooth and avoid any sudden jerks to prevent injury.
mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: Handstand Push-Up
secondaryMuscles: LATERAL DELTOID,TERES MAJOR,PECTORALIS MAJOR STERNAL HEAD
formTips: Slowly bend your elbows, lowering your body towards the floor in a controlled manner while keeping your core tight and your body straight.
steps: Slowly bend your elbows, lowering your body towards the floor in a controlled manner while keeping your core tight and your body straight.
Continue to lower yourself until your head lightly touches the ground or as far as your strength allows.
Then, push back up by straightening your arms, returning to the starting handstand position, while maintaining a rigid body line.
Repeat these steps for the desired number of reps, always ensuring to keep your movements controlled and your form correct.
mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: Jump Split
formTips: Bend your knees slightly and jump up, propelling yourself as high as you can.
steps: Bend your knees slightly and jump up, propelling yourself as high as you can.
While in the air, spread your legs apart into a split position, making sure to keep your core engaged and your back straight.
As you land, ensure to do so softly on the balls of your feet with your knees slightly bent to absorb the impact.
Return to the starting position and repeat the exercise for your desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: Standing One Arm Circling
formTips: Begin to move your arm in small circles, keeping your arm straight and your fingers extended.
steps: Begin to move your arm in small circles, keeping your arm straight and your fingers extended.
Gradually increase the size of the circles, ensuring your body remains stationary and only your arm is moving.
After a few moments, reverse the direction of the circles.
Repeat this exercise with the other arm.
mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: Commando Pull-up
formTips: Reach up and grip the bar with one hand closer to you and the other further away, in an overhand grip. Your hands should be shoulder-width apart, forming a line across your body.
steps: Reach up and grip the bar with one hand closer to you and the other further away, in an overhand grip. Your hands should be shoulder-width apart, forming a line across your body.
Pull your body up towards the bar while twisting your torso towards the hand that is closer to you. Your aim is to touch your shoulder to the bar.
Lower your body back down to the starting position in a controlled manner, ensuring to keep your body straight and not to swing.
Repeat the exercise on the other side by switching your hand positions and twisting your torso in the opposite direction.
mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: Forearm - Supination - Articulations
formTips: Hold a lightweight dumbbell vertically in your hand with your palm facing towards your body, which is the pronated position.
steps: Hold a lightweight dumbbell vertically in your hand with your palm facing towards your body, which is the pronated position.
Slowly rotate your forearm outward, turning the palm up, which is the supinated position, while keeping your elbow and upper arm stationary.
Hold this position for a few seconds to feel the contraction in your forearm.
Slowly return your forearm to the starting position and repeat the exercise for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: Sit
formTips: Position your feet flat on the floor, shoulder-width apart, and place your hands on your knees or thighs.
steps: Position your feet flat on the floor, shoulder-width apart, and place your hands on your knees or thighs.
Slowly lower your body down, bending at the hips and knees, until you're sitting upright with your back straight and shoulders relaxed.
Keep your feet firmly planted on the floor, and ensure your knees are not extending past your toes.
Hold this position for a moment, then slowly rise back to a standing position, keeping your back straight and using your legs to lift you. Repeat this process for the desired amount of reps.
mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: Neck Side Stretch
formTips: Maintain proper posture and controlled breathing.
steps: Maintain proper posture and controlled breathing.
mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: Standing Leg Calf Raise
formTips: Slowly raise your heels off the ground, putting your weight onto the balls of both feet.
steps: Slowly raise your heels off the ground, putting your weight onto the balls of both feet.
Ensure your abdominal muscles are engaged and your back is straight as you rise to your tiptoes.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, feeling the contraction in your calf muscles.
Slowly lower your heels back to the ground to complete one repetition, and repeat this process for your desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: Side Toe Touching
formTips: Bend at your waist to the right side, while keeping your back straight, and try to touch your right hand to your right foot, keeping your left hand raised.
steps: Bend at your waist to the right side, while keeping your back straight, and try to touch your right hand to your right foot, keeping your left hand raised.
Return to the original position slowly and repeat the same movement on the left side, trying to touch your left foot with your left hand while keeping your right hand raised.
This completes one repetition. Continue to alternate sides for your desired number of repetitions.
Remember to keep your movements controlled and smooth, avoiding any jerky motions to prevent injury.
mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: Seated Shoulder Flexor Depresor Retractor Stretch Bent Knee
formTips: Seated Shoulder Stretch: Sit up straight in a chair. Bring your left arm across your body and hold it with your right arm just above the elbow. Hold for 15-30 seconds, then switch sides.
steps: Seated Shoulder Stretch: Sit up straight in a chair. Bring your left arm across your body and hold it with your right arm just above the elbow. Hold for 15-30 seconds, then switch sides.

Shoulder Depressor (Scapular Depression): Stand tall with your arms by your sides. Without bending your arms, try to lower your shoulders down towards the ground as far as possible, then raise them up as high as possible.

name: Sissy Squat
formTips: Begin the movement by pushing your hips back and bending your knees, while simultaneously rising onto the balls of your feet. Keep your back straight and your chest up.
steps: Begin the movement by pushing your hips back and bending your knees, while simultaneously rising onto the balls of your feet. Keep your back straight and your chest up.
Lower your body as far as you can, ideally until your thighs are parallel to the floor, while keeping your heels off the ground. Your body should form a straight line from your head to your knees.
Hold the bottom position for a second, then push through the balls of your feet to rise back up to the starting position, keeping your body straight and your core engaged throughout the movement.
Repeat the exercise for the desired number of reps. Remember to keep a slow and controlled movement pace throughout the exercise to maximize muscle engagement.
mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: Downward Facing Dog
formTips: Lift your hips up towards the ceiling, straightening your legs and pushing your heels down towards the floor to form an inverted V shape with your body.
steps: Lift your hips up towards the ceiling, straightening your legs and pushing your heels down towards the floor to form an inverted V shape with your body.
Spread your fingers wide on the mat and press down through your palms, keeping your head between your arms and looking towards your knees.
Make sure your back is flat, and your weight is evenly distributed between your hands and feet.
Hold this position for a few breaths, then gently lower your body back to the starting position.
mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: Donkey Calf Raise
formTips: Position your feet shoulder-width apart on the platform, with your toes facing forward and your heels extending off the edge.
steps: Position your feet shoulder-width apart on the platform, with your toes facing forward and your heels extending off the edge.
Slowly lower your heels towards the ground, stretching your calf muscles as much as possible.
Then, push through the balls of both feet to raise your body upward, ensuring your knees are kept straight and your abdominal muscles are engaged.
Lower your heels back down slowly to the starting position and repeat the exercise for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: Wide Hand Push up
secondaryMuscles: ANTERIOR DELTOID,PECTORALIS MAJOR CLAVICULAR HEAD,TRICEPS BRACHII
formTips: Keep your body straight and rigid, from your head to your heels, engaging your core.
steps: Keep your body straight and rigid, from your head to your heels, engaging your core.
Lower your body towards the ground, bending your elbows out to the sides until your chest nearly touches the floor.
Pause for a moment at the bottom of the movement, ensuring your elbows are at a 90-degree angle.
Push your body back up to the starting position, extending your arms fully but without locking your elbows. Repeat the process for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: Right Hook. Boxing

formTips: Keep your fists up near your face for protection, with the right fist (or the one you're going to hook with) slightly behind.

Rotate your body to the right while pivoting on your back foot, this will give your punch power.
Swing your right fist in a hooking motion towards your target, keeping your elbow bent at a 90-degree angle and your palm facing down.

mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: Barbell Standing Calf Raise
formTips: Position your feet shoulder-width apart, with your toes pointing straight ahead or slightly outward.
steps: Position your feet shoulder-width apart, with your toes pointing straight ahead or slightly outward.
Slowly raise your heels off the ground, pushing up onto your toes while keeping your core engaged and your back straight.
Hold the position at the top for a moment, squeezing your calf muscles.
Slowly lower your heels back down to the ground, returning to the starting position. Repeat the movement for the desired number of reps.
mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: Circles Arm
formTips: Start to slowly make circles with your arms, keeping them straight and maintaining the shoulder height.
steps: Start to slowly make circles with your arms, keeping them straight and maintaining the shoulder height.
The direction of the circles can be forward or backward, and the size of the circles can vary from small to large.
Continue this movement for about 30 seconds to a minute, depending on your comfort level.
Rest and repeat the exercise for the desired number of sets, ensuring to alternate the direction of the circles with each set.
mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: Superman Row with Towel
formTips: Engage your core and lift your arms, chest, and legs off the ground, keeping your neck in a neutral position, this is your Superman pose.
steps: Engage your core and lift your arms, chest, and legs off the ground, keeping your neck in a neutral position, this is your Superman pose.
While maintaining this pose, pull the towel towards your chest by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together, this is your Row.
Extend your arms back out in front of you, still holding the towel, while maintaining your lifted position.
Lower your arms, chest, and legs back to the ground to complete one repetition, then repeat the sequence for your desired number of reps.
mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: Two Legs Reverse Biceps Curl with Towel

steps: Extend your arms fully in front of you at chest level, making sure the towel is taut between your hands.
Slowly curl your arms towards your chest while keeping your elbows stationary, pulling the towel as if you were trying to bend it in half, this will engage your biceps.
Hold this position for a few seconds to maximize muscle contraction, then slowly extend your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat this movement for the desired amount of repetitions, ensuring to keep the towel taut and your movements controlled throughout the exercise.
mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: Lying Double Legs Hammer Curl with Towel
formTips: Bend your knees and lift both legs off the floor, then loop the towel under your feet, holding one end of the towel in each hand.
steps: Bend your knees and lift both legs off the floor, then loop the towel under your feet, holding one end of the towel in each hand.
Keep your elbows close to your body and pull the towel towards your chest, curling your legs up as you do so, similar to a hammer curl with your legs.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, then slowly lower your legs back down to the starting position, keeping tension in the towel.
Repeat this exercise for the desired number of repetitions, ensuring to maintain proper form throughout.
mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: Dumbbell Clean and Press
formTips: Bend your knees slightly and using your whole body, lift the dumbbells up to your shoulders in a swift, clean motion, rotating your wrists so that your palms face forward.
steps: Bend your knees slightly and using your whole body, lift the dumbbells up to your shoulders in a swift, clean motion, rotating your wrists so that your palms face forward.
Once the dumbbells are at shoulder height, press them upward until your arms are fully extended, keeping your core engaged and your back straight.
Hold the position for a second, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to your shoulders.
Finally, bring the dumbbells back down to your sides in a controlled motion, completing one rep. Repeat this for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: L-Pull-up
formTips: Next, raise your legs parallel to the ground into an L-shape, keeping your legs straight and together; this is your starting position.
steps: Next, raise your legs parallel to the ground into an L-shape, keeping your legs straight and together; this is your starting position.
Using your upper body strength, pull yourself up until your chin is above the bar, while maintaining the L-shape with your legs.
Hold this position for a moment, ensuring your core is engaged and your body is in a straight line.
Finally, lower yourself back down in a controlled manner to the starting position, keeping your legs in the L-shape throughout the exercise.
mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: Bench Press
secondaryMuscles: TRICEPS BRACHII,ANTERIOR DELTOID,PECTORALIS MAJOR CLAVICULAR HEAD
formTips: Grip the barbell with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, palms facing your feet, and lift it off the rack, holding it straight over your chest with your arms fully extended.
steps: Grip the barbell with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, palms facing your feet, and lift it off the rack, holding it straight over your chest with your arms fully extended.
Slowly lower the barbell down to your chest while keeping your elbows at a 90-degree angle.
Once the barbell touches your chest, push it back up to the starting position while keeping your back flat on the bench.
Repeat this process for the desired number of repetitions, always maintaining control of the barbell and ensuring your form is correct.
mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: Biceps Leg Concentration Curl

Hold the position for a second, feeling the tension in your biceps.
Lower the dumbbell back down to the starting position, making sure to keep the movement controlled. Repeat the exercise for your desired number of repetitions and then switch to the other arm.
mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: Front Plank
formTips: Push your body up onto your forearms and toes, making sure your elbows are directly under your shoulders and your forearms are facing forward.
steps: Push your body up onto your forearms and toes, making sure your elbows are directly under your shoulders and your forearms are facing forward.
Keep your body in a straight line from your head to your feet, ensuring your back is flat and your hips are not dropping or rising.
Engage your core muscles and hold this position for as long as you can, ideally aiming for 30 seconds to 1 minute.
Lower your body back to the starting position in a controlled manner and repeat the exercise as desired.
mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: Step-up on Chair
formTips: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, facing the chair.
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, facing the chair.
Step up onto the chair with your right foot, pressing down while bringing your left foot to meet your right so you are standing on the chair.
Carefully step back down, starting with your right foot, then bringing your left foot down to meet the right, returning to your original standing position.
Repeat this movement, alternating the leading foot each time to ensure balanced exercise for both sides of your body.
mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: Hip Thrusts
formTips: Roll the bar so that it is directly above your hips, and lean back against the bench so that your shoulder blades are near the top of it.
steps: Roll the bar so that it is directly above your hips, and lean back against the bench so that your shoulder blades are near the top of it.
Begin the movement by driving through your feet, extending your hips vertically through the bar, and ensure your weight is supported by your shoulder blades and your feet.
Extend as far as possible, then reverse the motion to return to the starting position.
Repeat the process for the desired amount of repetitions, ensuring to keep your chin tucked and not to hyperextend your back at the top of the movement.
mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: Stationary Bike Run
formTips: Once you're seated, place your feet onto the pedals and hold onto the handles of the bike, maintaining a relaxed grip.
steps: Once you're seated, place your feet onto the pedals and hold onto the handles of the bike, maintaining a relaxed grip.
Set your desired resistance level on the bike's monitor, starting with a lower level if you're a beginner and gradually increasing the resistance as you get more comfortable.
Begin pedaling at a steady pace, keeping your back straight and your abs engaged, ensuring that you are breathing normally.
Continue this exercise for a set duration of time or until you've reached your desired distance, then gradually slow down your pedaling to cool down.
mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: Elbow Up and Down Dynamic Plank
formTips: Push up from the ground one arm at a time into a push-up position, keeping your body as stable and straight as possible.
steps: Push up from the ground one arm at a time into a push-up position, keeping your body as stable and straight as possible.
Once you're in the push-up position, lower yourself back down one arm at a time to the original plank position.
Ensure that your core is engaged and your back is straight throughout the exercise to maintain proper form.
Repeat this movement for a set number of repetitions or for a specific time period, remembering to alternate the arm you start with each time.
mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: Dumbbell One Arm Bent-over Row
formTips: Bend your knees slightly and lean forward from your waist until your torso is almost parallel to the floor, making sure to keep your back straight.
steps: Bend your knees slightly and lean forward from your waist until your torso is almost parallel to the floor, making sure to keep your back straight.
Hold onto the bench with your free hand for support, and let the hand holding the dumbbell hang down from your shoulder.
Pull the dumbbell up towards your waist, keeping your elbow close to your body and squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Lower the dumbbell back down in a controlled manner to the starting position, and repeat the exercise for your desired number of reps before switching to the other arm.
mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: Sumo Squat
formTips: Lower your body by bending your knees and hips, keeping your back straight and your chest upright, as if you're trying to sit between your legs.
steps: Lower your body by bending your knees and hips, keeping your back straight and your chest upright, as if you're trying to sit between your legs.
Continue to lower yourself until your thighs are parallel to the floor, ensuring your knees are directly above your ankles.
Pause for a moment at the bottom of the squat, keeping your core engaged.
Push through your heels to return to the starting position, straightening your legs and squeezing your glutes at the top of the movement.
mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: Standing Arms Flinging
formTips: Swiftly swing both arms up above your head, keeping them straight and parallel to each other.
steps: Swiftly swing both arms up above your head, keeping them straight and parallel to each other.
Once your arms reach their highest point, quickly swing them back down to your sides.
As your arms reach your sides, continue the momentum to swing them behind your body as far as you comfortably can.
Return to the starting position and repeat the exercise for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: Dumbbell Rear Delt Fly

steps: Bend forward at the waist so your chest is leaning forward over your feet. Keep your back straight and let your arms hang straight down, palms facing each other.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows and raise your arms out to the sides until they're at shoulder level, like you're spreading your wings. This is the fly part of the exercise.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat this movement for your desired number of repetitions, remembering to keep your core engaged and back straight throughout the exercise.
mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: Kneeling Toe Up Hamstring Stretch

steps: Slowly extend the front leg straight out in front of you, keeping your foot flat on the ground.
Carefully lift the toes of the extended leg towards the ceiling, keeping your heel on the ground, until you feel a stretch in the back of your thigh.
Hold this position, ensuring your back is straight and your hips are square, for 20 to 30 seconds to allow the hamstring muscle to stretch.

mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: Two Front Toe Touching

steps: Lift your right leg straight out in front of you while keeping your left foot firmly on the ground.

name: Lunge

steps: Take a big step forward with your right foot, keeping your left foot in place.
Lower your body until your right knee forms a 90-degree angle, making sure your right knee is directly above your right ankle and your left knee is hovering just above the floor.
Push off your right foot to return to the starting position.
Repeat the movement with your left leg, alternating legs for each repetition.

name: Dumbbell Decline One Arm Hammer Press

formTips: Hold a dumbbell in one hand with a neutral grip (palms facing inward), at chest level, fully extending your arm upward to prepare for the press.
steps: Hold a dumbbell in one hand with a neutral grip (palms facing inward), at chest level, fully extending your arm upward to prepare for the press.
Slowly lower the dumbbell towards your chest, keeping your elbow close to your body and ensuring that your wrist stays straight.
Once the dumbbell is near your chest, push it back up to the starting position, fully extending your arm but not locking your elbow.

mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: Inverted Chin Curl with Bent Knee between Chairs

Push yourself back up to the starting position by straightening your arms, ensuring to keep your body straight and your core engaged throughout the movement. Repeat this exercise for the desired number of repetitions.

steps: Maintain proper posture and controlled breathing.

steps: Extend one arm out straight, then bend it at the elbow and reach it behind your head and down your back as far as you can.
With your other arm, reach behind your back and try to grab the fingers of your extended arm.
Once you've clasped your fingers, gently pull the top arm downwards to deepen the stretch, holding for 15-30 seconds.
Release the stretch, switch arms, and repeat the process.
mistakes: Using momentum or rushing eccentric phase.

name: Butt Kicks
formTips: Start jogging in place, lifting your heels as high as they can go, aiming to kick your glutes with your heels on each lift.

Make sure your knees are pointing towards the floor as you lift your legs, not out in front.
Continue this exercise for a set amount of time, usually around 30 seconds to a minute, depending on your fitness level.

name: Feet and Ankles Side to Side Stretch

name: Pec Deck Machine Fly

steps: Sit on the pec deck machine and adjust the seat so your arms are parallel to the floor.
Place your forearms against the arm pads or grip the handles with elbows bent at 90 degrees.
Press the arm pads together in front of your chest by contracting your pectoral muscles.
Pause at the peak of the contraction and squeeze your chest.
Slowly allow the arm pads to return to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Svend Press Chest
formTips: Stand upright and hold a pair of weight plates pressed together at chest level with both palms.
steps: Stand upright and hold a pair of weight plates pressed together at chest level with both palms.
Press the plates outward from your chest until your arms are nearly fully extended.
Squeeze the plates together throughout the entire movement to engage the inner chest.
Slowly pull the plates back towards your chest in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Air Bike Sprint
formTips: Sit on the air bike and adjust the seat so your legs are slightly bent at full extension.
steps: Sit on the air bike and adjust the seat so your legs are slightly bent at full extension.
Grip the moving handles with both hands.
Begin pedaling and pumping the handles simultaneously at maximum effort.
Sprint at full intensity for the desired interval duration.
Slow down gradually and rest before repeating.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Barbell Back Squat
formTips: Position a barbell on your upper traps and step back from the rack with feet shoulder-width apart.
steps: Position a barbell on your upper traps and step back from the rack with feet shoulder-width apart.
Point your toes slightly outward and keep your chest up and core braced.
Descend by bending your knees and pushing your hips back until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Drive through your heels to extend your knees and hips and return to the standing position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Barbell Bulgarian Split Squat
formTips: Stand in front of a bench and hold a barbell across your upper traps.
steps: Stand in front of a bench and hold a barbell across your upper traps.
Extend one leg behind you and rest the top of your foot on the bench.
Lower your back knee toward the floor by bending your front knee, keeping your torso upright.
Descend until your front thigh is parallel to the floor.
Drive through your front heel to return to the starting position and repeat, then switch legs.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Barbell Front Squat
formTips: Position a barbell in a front rack across the front of your shoulders with your elbows raised high.
steps: Position a barbell in a front rack across the front of your shoulders with your elbows raised high.
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and toes slightly pointed out.
Keeping your elbows high and torso upright, descend by bending your knees and hips.
Lower until your thighs are parallel to the floor or below.
Drive through your heels to return to the standing position and repeat.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Barbell March
formTips: Hold a barbell across your upper traps as in a back squat position with feet hip-width apart.
steps: Hold a barbell across your upper traps as in a back squat position with feet hip-width apart.
Brace your core and maintain an upright posture.
Lift one knee upward to hip height in a marching motion while keeping your stance foot flat.
Lower your foot and repeat the movement with the opposite leg.
Continue alternating legs in a controlled marching motion for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Barbell Reverse Lunges
formTips: Stand upright with a barbell across your upper traps and feet together.
steps: Stand upright with a barbell across your upper traps and feet together.
Step one foot directly backward and lower your back knee toward the floor.
Continue descending until your front thigh is parallel to the floor.
Push through your front heel to bring your back foot forward to the starting position.
Alternate legs for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Barbell Romanian Deadlift
formTips: Stand with feet hip-width apart holding a barbell in front of your thighs with an overhand grip.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart holding a barbell in front of your thighs with an overhand grip.
Keep a soft bend in your knees and your back flat throughout the movement.
Hinge at the hips and push them back as you lower the bar along your legs.
Continue lowering until you feel a deep stretch in your hamstrings.
Drive your hips forward to return to the upright position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Cable Leg Kickback
formTips: Attach an ankle strap to the low pulley of a cable machine and secure it to one ankle.
steps: Attach an ankle strap to the low pulley of a cable machine and secure it to one ankle.
Face the machine and hold the frame for support, keeping your body slightly inclined.
Keeping your knee straight, kick your strapped leg backward and upward as far as possible.
Squeeze your glute at the top of the movement.
Slowly return your leg to the starting position and repeat, then switch legs.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Cycling
formTips: Mount a stationary bike and adjust the seat height so your leg has a slight bend at full pedal extension.
steps: Mount a stationary bike and adjust the seat height so your leg has a slight bend at full pedal extension.
Place your feet in the pedal straps and grip the handlebars.
Begin pedaling at a comfortable cadence, maintaining an upright or forward-leaning posture.
Adjust the resistance as needed to reach your target intensity level.
Continue for the desired duration, then gradually slow to a cool down pace.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Dumbbell Bulgarian Split Squat
formTips: Stand in front of a bench and hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
steps: Stand in front of a bench and hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Extend one leg back and rest the top of your foot on the bench.
Lower your back knee toward the floor by bending your front knee.
Descend until your front thigh is parallel to the floor.
Drive through your front heel to return to the starting position and repeat, then switch legs.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Dumbbell Goblet Squat
formTips: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart holding a dumbbell vertically at chest level with both hands cupping the top end.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart holding a dumbbell vertically at chest level with both hands cupping the top end.
Keep your elbows tucked in and your chest up.
Descend into a squat by bending your knees and pushing your hips back until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Drive through your heels to return to the standing position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Dumbbell Hip Hinge
formTips: Stand with feet hip-width apart holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Keep a slight bend in your knees and your back flat throughout the movement.
Hinge at the hips and push them back as you lower your torso toward the floor.
Lower until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings, then drive your hips forward to return to standing.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Dumbbell Jump Squat
formTips: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart holding a light dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart holding a light dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Perform a squat by bending your knees and pushing your hips back to thigh-parallel depth.
Explosively drive through your heels to jump off the ground as high as possible.
Land softly with bent knees to absorb the impact.
Immediately descend into the next squat and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Elliptical Hiit Machine
formTips: Step onto the elliptical machine and grip the moving handles.
steps: Step onto the elliptical machine and grip the moving handles.
Set a high resistance level appropriate for interval training.
Push and pull the handles while driving through the pedals at maximum effort for the work interval.
Reduce your pace to a slow recovery stride for the rest interval.
Continue alternating between work and rest intervals for the desired duration.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Kettlebell Hold March
formTips: Stand upright holding a kettlebell in each hand at your sides.
steps: Stand upright holding a kettlebell in each hand at your sides.
Brace your core and maintain an upright posture with shoulders back.
Lift one knee upward to hip height in a controlled marching motion.
Lower that foot to the floor and immediately lift the opposite knee.
Continue alternating legs in a slow, deliberate march for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Kettlebell Lift Up
formTips: Stand with feet hip-width apart and a kettlebell on the floor between your feet.
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart and a kettlebell on the floor between your feet.
Hinge at the hips and bend your knees to grip the kettlebell handle with both hands.
Brace your core and maintain a flat back as you prepare to lift.
Drive through your heels and extend your hips and knees to stand upright, lifting the kettlebell.
Lower the kettlebell back to the floor in a controlled manner and repeat.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Kettlebell Swing
formTips: Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulder-width and the kettlebell on the floor in front of you.
steps: Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulder-width and the kettlebell on the floor in front of you.
Hinge at the hips to grip the kettlebell with both hands and hike it back between your legs.
Explosively drive your hips forward to propel the kettlebell upward to chest or shoulder height.
Allow the kettlebell to swing back down and hike it back between your legs, hinging at the hips.
Repeat the swing in a fluid, continuous motion for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Leg Press Machine
formTips: Sit on the leg press machine and place your feet shoulder-width apart on the platform.
steps: Sit on the leg press machine and place your feet shoulder-width apart on the platform.
Release the safety handles and lower the platform by bending your knees toward your chest.
Stop when your knees reach approximately 90 degrees or your lower back begins to lift off the seat.
Drive through your heels to extend your knees and push the platform back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Rope Wave
formTips: Hold one end of a battle rope in each hand and stand in a half-squat position.
steps: Hold one end of a battle rope in each hand and stand in a half-squat position.
Brace your core and keep your feet shoulder-width apart.
Rapidly raise and lower one arm while the other arm descends, creating alternating waves in the rope.
Maintain a continuous, powerful wave motion for the desired interval duration.
Rest and repeat for the desired number of sets.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Rowing Machine
formTips: Sit on the rowing machine, secure your feet in the straps, and grip the handle with both hands.
steps: Sit on the rowing machine, secure your feet in the straps, and grip the handle with both hands.
Begin with your knees bent, leaning slightly forward, and arms extended.
Drive through your legs to extend your knees while simultaneously leaning back slightly.
As your legs reach full extension, pull the handle toward your lower chest by bending your elbows.
Reverse the sequence to return to the starting position and repeat for the desired duration.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Seated Overhead Press
formTips: Sit on a shoulder press machine and adjust the seat so the handles are at shoulder height.
steps: Sit on a shoulder press machine and adjust the seat so the handles are at shoulder height.
Grip the handles with both hands and plant your feet flat on the floor.
Press the handles upward until your arms are fully extended overhead.
Pause briefly at the top, then slowly lower the handles back to shoulder height.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Step-Ups (Weighted)
formTips: Stand in front of a box or bench holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
steps: Stand in front of a box or bench holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Step one foot up onto the surface and drive through that heel to lift your body up.
Bring your back foot up to stand fully on the box.
Step the leading foot back down to the floor followed by the trailing foot.
Alternate the leading leg or complete all repetitions on one side before switching.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Stepmill Machine Version 1
formTips: Step onto the stepmill machine and grip the handrails lightly for balance.
steps: Step onto the stepmill machine and grip the handrails lightly for balance.
Set your desired speed on the control panel.
Begin stepping at a comfortable pace, placing your full foot on each step.
Drive through your heel with each step to engage your glutes and quads.
Continue for the desired duration, maintaining an upright posture and minimizing reliance on the handrails.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Stepmill Machine
formTips: Mount the stepmill and set your target speed and duration.
steps: Mount the stepmill and set your target speed and duration.
Step onto the rotating staircase and begin climbing at a steady pace.
Keep your torso upright and engage your core throughout the exercise.
Drive through each step using your full foot to activate the glutes and quads.
Complete the session for the desired duration, then slow down to cool off before dismounting.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Stiff-Legged Deadlift Machine
formTips: Stand on the platform of a deadlift machine with feet hip-width apart and grip the handles.
steps: Stand on the platform of a deadlift machine with feet hip-width apart and grip the handles.
Keep your legs nearly straight with a slight bend in your knees.
Hinge at the hips and lower the handles along your legs until you feel a deep hamstring stretch.
Drive your hips forward to return to the upright starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Triceps Pushdown (Cable - Rope)
formTips: Attach a rope handle to the high pulley of a cable machine and stand facing the machine.
steps: Attach a rope handle to the high pulley of a cable machine and stand facing the machine.
Grasp the rope with both hands using a neutral grip and tuck your elbows close to your sides.
Push the rope downward by extending your arms until they are fully straight.
At the bottom, spread the rope ends apart slightly to maximize tricep contraction.
Slowly allow the rope to rise back to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Walk On Treadmill
formTips: Step onto the treadmill and set a comfortable walking speed and incline.
steps: Step onto the treadmill and set a comfortable walking speed and incline.
Begin walking at your chosen pace, maintaining an upright posture.
Swing your arms naturally in coordination with your stride.
Keep your gaze forward and avoid looking down at your feet.
Continue walking for the desired duration, then gradually bring the belt to a stop.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Arnold Press Dumbbell
formTips: Sit on a bench with back support and hold a dumbbell in each hand at chest height, palms facing you.
steps: Sit on a bench with back support and hold a dumbbell in each hand at chest height, palms facing you.
Begin the press by rotating your palms to face forward as you push the dumbbells upward.
Continue pressing until your arms are fully extended overhead.
Reverse the motion, rotating your palms back to face you as you lower the dumbbells to chest height.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Barbell Overhead Press Standing
formTips: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and hold a barbell at shoulder height with an overhand grip.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and hold a barbell at shoulder height with an overhand grip.
Brace your core and maintain a neutral spine throughout the movement.
Press the barbell directly overhead until your arms are fully extended.
Pause at the top, then slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Barbell Upright Row
formTips: Stand upright holding a barbell with an overhand grip, hands approximately shoulder-width apart.
steps: Stand upright holding a barbell with an overhand grip, hands approximately shoulder-width apart.
Let the bar hang in front of your thighs with your arms extended.
Pull the bar upward along your body by raising your elbows above the level of your hands.
Continue pulling until the bar reaches chin height and your elbows are above your shoulders.
Slowly lower the bar back to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Dumbbell Overhead Standard
formTips: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, palms facing forward.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, palms facing forward.
Brace your core and maintain an upright posture.
Press the dumbbells upward until your arms are fully extended overhead.
Pause briefly at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to shoulder height.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Dumbbell Upright Row
formTips: Stand upright holding a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip in front of your thighs.
steps: Stand upright holding a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip in front of your thighs.
Pull the dumbbells upward along your body by raising your elbows above the level of your hands.
Continue pulling until the dumbbells reach chest height and your elbows are at shoulder level.
Pause at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Front Raise (Dumbbell)
formTips: Stand upright holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs with palms facing your body.
steps: Stand upright holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs with palms facing your body.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows and your back straight.
Raise one or both dumbbells forward and upward until your arms are parallel to the floor.
Pause briefly at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Front Raise (Weighted Plate)
formTips: Stand upright and hold a weight plate with both hands at the 3 and 9 o'clock positions in front of your thighs.
steps: Stand upright and hold a weight plate with both hands at the 3 and 9 o'clock positions in front of your thighs.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows and your core engaged.
Raise the plate forward and upward in a controlled arc until your arms are parallel to the floor.
Pause briefly at the top, then slowly lower the plate back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Kettlebell Overhead Press
formTips: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and hold a kettlebell in one hand at shoulder height in the rack position.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and hold a kettlebell in one hand at shoulder height in the rack position.
Brace your core and keep your elbow pointing forward.
Press the kettlebell straight overhead until your arm is fully extended.
Pause at the top, then slowly lower the kettlebell back to the rack position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Cable Cross Lateral Raise
formTips: Stand between two low cable pulleys and grasp the opposite handle with each hand so the cables cross in front of your body.
steps: Stand between two low cable pulleys and grasp the opposite handle with each hand so the cables cross in front of your body.
Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart, keep your core braced, and maintain a slight bend in your elbows.
Raise both arms out to your sides until they are approximately parallel to the floor.
Pause briefly at the top while squeezing your lateral deltoids.
Slowly lower the handles back to the starting position under control and repeat.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Lateral Raises (Dumbbell)
formTips: Stand upright holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with a neutral grip.
steps: Stand upright holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with a neutral grip.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows and your core engaged.
Raise both dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc until your arms are parallel to the floor.
Pause briefly at the top and squeeze your medial delts.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Lateral Raise Machine
formTips: Stand on the platform of the lateral raise machine and position your upper arms against the pads.
steps: Stand on the platform of the lateral raise machine and position your upper arms against the pads.
Keep your chest up, core engaged, and maintain a slight bend in your elbows.
Raise the pads outward by abducting your shoulders until your upper arms are approximately parallel to the floor.
Pause briefly at the top and squeeze your lateral deltoids.
Slowly lower the weight back to the starting position under control and repeat.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Military Press (Seated - Smith Machine)
formTips: Set a bench inside a smith machine and adjust the bar to shoulder height.
steps: Set a bench inside a smith machine and adjust the bar to shoulder height.
Sit on the bench and grip the bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Unrack the bar and hold it at the front of your shoulders.
Press the bar upward until your arms are fully extended overhead.
Slowly lower the bar back to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Rear Delt Fly (Reverse Pec Deck)
formTips: Sit facing the pec deck machine and adjust the seat so your arms are parallel to the floor.
steps: Sit facing the pec deck machine and adjust the seat so your arms are parallel to the floor.
Grip the handles with a neutral grip and keep a slight bend in your elbows.
Pull the handles outward and backward in a wide arcing motion by squeezing your rear delts and shoulder blades together.
Pause at the peak of the contraction.
Slowly return the handles to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.

name: Rear Delt Cable Fly
formTips: Stand between two cable pulleys set at shoulder height.
steps: Stand between two cable pulleys set at shoulder height.
Grasp the opposite cable handle with each hand and step back until there is tension on the cables.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbows and keep your chest up throughout the movement.
Pull your arms outward and backward in a wide arc until they are in line with your shoulders.
Squeeze your rear delts and upper back at the end of the movement.
Slowly return to the starting position under control and repeat.
mistakes: Rushing repetitions and losing eccentric cadence control.
Failing to maintain proper core bracing and spinal alignment.
